{{Short description|American computer security specialist}}
{{BLP sources|date=March 2011}}
'''John Viega''' (born February 22, 1974) is an American [[computer security]] author, researcher and professional.

==Early life==
John Viega earned his BA from the [[University of Virginia]]. As an undergraduate, he worked in [[Randy Pausch]]'s Stage 3 Research Group, as an early contributor to [[Alice (software)|Alice]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.cs.cmu.edu/~jpierce/publications/chialice.pdf |title=Alice: Lessons Learned from Building a 3D System For Novices |last1=Conway |first1=Matthew |year=2000 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20010616005041/https://www.cs.cmu.edu/~jpierce/publications/chialice.pdf |archivedate=2001-06-16 }}</ref>  Viega earned an MS in [[Computer science|Computer Science]], also from the University of Virginia.<ref name="auto">{{cite conference |url=https://www.usenix.org/legacy/publications/library/proceedings/lisa98/full_papers/viega/viega_html/viega.html |title=Mailman: The Gnu Mailing List Manager |last1=Viega |first1=John |last2=Warsaw |first2=Barry |last3=Manheimer |first3=Ken |date=1998-12-09 |location=Boston, Ma |conference=12th Systems Administration Conference (LISA '98)}}</ref>

While at the University of Virginia, Viega started a popular mailing list for the [[Dave Matthews Band]].<ref>{{cite book |last1=Brown |first1=Amy |last2=Wilson |first2=Brown |date=2012-03-30 |title=The Architecture of Open Source Applications, Volume II |publisher=Lulu |page=149 |url=https://aosabook.org/en/ |isbn=978-1105571817}}</ref> Frustrated by the maintenance costs for a large, active mailing list, he wrote the first version of [[GNU Mailman]], which quickly took off, leading the shift of mailing list management from email commands to the web.<ref name="auto"/>

==Career==
Viega co-authored Building Secure Software<ref>{{cite book |last1=Viega |first1=John |last2=McGraw |first2=Gary |date=2001-09-24 |title=Building Secure Software |publisher=Addison Wesley |isbn=978-0321774958}}</ref> (Addison Wesley, 2001), which was the first book to teach developers about writing secure software. He has since co-authored a number of additional books on computer security, including Network Security with OpenSSL<ref>{{cite book |last1=Viega |first1=John |last2=Messier |first2=Matt |last3=Chandra |first3=Pravir |date=2002-06-15 |title=Network Security with OpenSSL |publisher=O'Reilly Media |isbn=978-0596002701}}</ref> (O'Reilly, 2002), the Secure Programming Cookbook<ref>{{cite book |last1=Viega |first1=John |last2=Messier |first2=Matt |date=2003-08-19 |title=Secure Programming Cookbook for C and C++ |publisher=O'Reilly Media |isbn=978-0596003944}}</ref> (O'Reilly, 2003), Beautiful Security <ref>{{cite book |last1=Oram |first1=Andy |last2=Viega |first2=John |date=2009-07-02 |title=Beautiful Security: Leading Security Experts Explain How They Think |publisher=O'Reilly Media |isbn=978-0596527488}}</ref> (O'Reilly, 2009), and the 19 Deadly Sins of Software Security <ref>{{cite book |last1=Howard |first1=Michael |last2=LeBlanc |first2=David |last3=Viega |first3=John |date=2005-07-26 |title=19 Deadly Sins of Software Security |publisher=McGraw-Hill Osborne Media |isbn=978-0072260854}}</ref> (McGraw Hill, 2005)

In 2005, he co-authored the widely used [[GCM mode]] of operation for AES, along with [[David A. McGrew]],<ref>{{cite web |url=http://csrc.nist.gov/groups/ST/toolkit/BCM/documents/proposedmodes/gcm/gcm-spec.pdf |title=The Galois/Counter Mode of Operation (GCM) |last1=McGrew |first1=David A. |last2=Viega |first2=John |authorlink2=John Viega |page=5 |year=2005}}</ref> which was designed to provide both encryption and authentication with one primitive that is both cost-effective in hardware, and unencumbered by patents.

Viega was also a pioneer in static analysis for security vulnerabilities. He was responsible for ITS4,<ref>{{cite book|url=http://dl.acm.org/citation.cfm?id=784591.784731|title=ITS4: A Static Vulnerability Scanner for C and C++ Code|first1=J.|last1=Viega|first2=J. T.|last2=Bloch|first3=Y.|last3=Kohno|first4=G.|last4=McGraw|date=29 December 2018|publisher=IEEE Computer Society|pages=257–|isbn=9780769508597 |accessdate=29 December 2018|via=ACM Digital Library}}</ref> the first static analysis tool in this class. He co-founded Secure Software, the first commercial vendor for such tools, which also released an open source tool, Rough Auditing Tool for Security (RATS).

At the end of 2005, Viega left Secure Software and joined [[McAfee]], first as Chief Security Architect, and later as CTO, SaaS. Secure Software was bought by [[Fortify Software]] just over a year later.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.infoworld.com/article/2660997/techology-business/fortify-buys-secure-software.html|title=Fortify buys Secure Software|first=Robert|last=McMillan|date=17 January 2007|website=InfoWorld.com|accessdate=29 December 2018}}</ref>

Post-McAfee, he was an executive at SilverSky, a cloud security provider funded by [[Goldman Sachs]] and [[Bessemer Venture Partners]], which was acquired by [[BAE Systems]] in 2014,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.law360.com/articles/588808/bae-closes-233m-deal-for-cybersecurity-co-silversky|title=BAE Closes $233M Deal For Cybersecurity Co. SilverSky - Law360|author=Andrew Westney|website=Law360.com|accessdate=29 December 2018}}</ref> where he was Executive Vice President of Products and Engineering.

In 2016, he left to co-found Capsule8 with [[Dino Dai-Zovi]] and Brandon Edwards, which was acquired by [[Sophos]] in July 2021.<ref>{{cite press release|url=https://www.globenewswire.com/en/news-release/2021/07/07/2259059/0/en/Sophos-Acquires-Capsule8-to-Bring-Powerful-and-Lightweight-Linux-Server-and-Cloud-Container-Security-to-its-Adaptive-Cybersecurity-Ecosystem-ACE.html|title=Sophos Acquires Capsule8 to Bring Powerful and Lightweight Linux Server and Cloud Container Security to its Adaptive Cybersecurity Ecosystem...|author=Sophos Inc.|website=globenewswire.com|date=2021-07-07 |accessdate=2023-11-30}}</ref>

Viega was also the lead author of [[OWASP]]'s CLASP,<ref>{{cite conference|title=Building Security Requirements with CLASP|first=John|last=Viega|doi=10.1145/1083200.1083207|date=May 2005|conference=ACM 2005 workshop on Software engineering for secure systems—building trustworthy applications|book-title=Proceedings of the 2005 workshop on Software engineering for secure systems—building trustworthy applications}}</ref>  a lightweight process for relating software development to security. He is also a former editor-in-chief for the IEEE Security & Privacy Magazine. He has been an adjunct professor at Virginia Tech, and New York University.<ref>{{cite podcast |url= https://zero2exit.podcastpage.io/episode/academia-to-entrepreneurship-john-viega-founder-ceo-capsule8 |title=Zero To Exit |host=Ankur Shah and Neelima Rustagi |date=2021-07-29 |accessdate=2023-11-30}}</ref>

Viega is currently the lead developer for the open source software provenance and observability tool, Chalk, as well as the co-founder and CEO of Crash Override.<ref>{{cite podcast |url= https://appsec.buzzsprout.com/1730684/13527225 |title=The Application Security Podcast |host=Chris Romeo and Robert Hurlbut |date=2023-07-29 |accessdate=2023-09-05}}</ref>
